questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road that faces the traffic coming toward you.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?

options.text: Enter the far-right lane right away and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: Wait for a gap in traffic to appear before speeding up and entering the interstate.

questions.question: How should you make room for cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Change to a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Merge into another lane if possible to create space for cars entering the freeway. If you cannot merge, adjust your speed to let them enter safely.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks side by side, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to go after one train passes.
Always stop before crossing.
Look for a second train on the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for a second train on the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: After one train passes, check the other track for a second train. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming on either track.

questions.question: How far from a fire hydrant can you not park?

options.text: 10 feet
25 feet
50 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 feet
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 50 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Start signaling as you move to the next lane.
Signal 500 feet ahead on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Cars and motorcycles can hide there. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes on residential streets. Signal 5 seconds ahead on freeways.

questions.question: When a vehicle's high beams are coming toward you, where should you look?

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded. This lets you see the road and stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their high beams. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid the glare. This helps you see enough to stay on your course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: How can you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep looking at the centerline.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Glance toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights. Then continue looking ahead to see where the other vehicle is.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers pull behind large vehicles before passing.
Because following too close will trap you in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles block the driver's side view, so they may not see you directly behind them. Increase your distance to see around the vehicle and view the road ahead.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning when driving in rain?

options.text: Drive at the speed you would use in good weather.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast in wet conditions, your tires lose contact with the road. Your car rides on top of the water instead. This is called hydroplaning. The best way to prevent it is to drive slower in rain or wet conditions.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.
Look to the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the left and right sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At any place where people may cross or traffic meets, look left and right to make sure nothing is coming.

questions.question: When you arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as other vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until there are no vehicles before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or signals, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Drivers then proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly in a car without Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should:

options.text: Hold down the brake pedal.
Pump your brakes firmly.
Lightly tap the brakes.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump your brakes firmly.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop a car in an emergency. Your car will stop quickly and you can still steer.

questions.question: When a curb is painted ____, it means you can only park for a short time.

options.text: Yellow
Blue
White
Red

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Painted curbs show parking rules. A white curb means only short stops are allowed.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dim street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
Use high beam headlights to see vehicles ahead better.
Keep instrument panel lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area your headlights illuminate.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator is stuck open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on your brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off your ignition without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When the accelerator sticks, the car will keep going fast even if you lift your foot off the gas. Turn off the ignition carefully so the steering wheel does not lock. Then apply your brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway or to make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and quickly.
Always stop before crossing.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to cross before any train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be prepared to stop for any train at a railroad crossing, especially if there are no lights or gates. Make sure your entire vehicle can fit on the other side of the tracks before crossing. Do not shift gears while crossing because your car might stall.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right for road construction.
The road ahead makes a sharp turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead makes a sharp turn.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about road conditions ahead. This sign tells you to slow down and prepare for a sharp turn in the road.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, you should:

options.text: Pass them on the right.
Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
Follow closer behind them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks must stop at railroad crossings. Be ready to stop if you are following one of these vehicles.

questions.question: At intersections with a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Let cross traffic go first if it is close enough to be a problem.
Let vehicles on your right go first only.
Always slow down and go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let cross traffic go first if it is close enough to be a problem.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Let other vehicles go first if they are close enough to cause a collision.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, you should slow down:

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
When you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Get into the exit lane early. Do not slow down until after you have moved into the exit lane.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn. You should:

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to get other drivers to let you through.
Drive around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If a car hits you from behind, this stops you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.
